title: Knowledge check: Monitoring and Production Maintenance

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Monitoring and Production Maintenance”?
options: SSG output changes automatically on every API update without rebuilding.
A local development server proves production hosting routes work.
SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
window is available while rendering on every server.
questions.answer_key: SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Monitoring and Production Maintenance directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Runtime error logging”, which practice is most reliable?
options: A local development server proves production hosting routes work.
SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
window is available while rendering on every server.
SSG output changes automatically on every API update without rebuilding.
questions.answer_key: SSR output should hydrate deterministically and mutable state must not be unintentionally shared across requests.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Runtime error logging”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

questions.prompt: A learner example for “Monitoring and Production Maintenance” behaves unexpectedly. What should be checked first?
options: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
Change unrelated files until the page looks correct.
Disable error handling and assume the framework is at fault.
Trust a client-supplied success flag without checking behavior.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
